hema rao: FYI bringing up Cetus-11B (partner checkpoint) on int4. Quick smoke shows token-id shift + rotary-angle mismatch vs our Gemma baseline — outputs truncate around ~1200 tokens sometimes. Anyone seen this pattern?

matt besser: :eyes: can you paste the exact conversion command you used?

hema rao: converter command I ran: 
```
./model_convert --from=hf --to=redwood --model=cetus-11b --vocab-map=auto --rotary-merge=auto --out=cetus-redwood.bin
```

leo wang: hmm, that `--rotary-merge=auto` can pick scalar vs headwise heuristics. Try `--rotary-merge=headwise` — we saw drift when auto picked scalar for heterogenous head dims.

sana li: Also double-check special sentinel token ids. We had one conversion flip byte-order and special tokens got remapped. Quick diff example: 
```
orig_vocab[5023] = 0x01F3 -> "\u00A0" (NBSP)
conv_vocab[5023] = 0x03F1 -> "" (empty)
```

hema rao: Repro command I'm using for bench: 
```
eval_harness --model ./cetus-redwood.bin --task longctx-summary --max-tokens 2048 --seed 42
```
Results vs fp16 baseline: PPL_fp16=6.8  PPL_int4=9.4  ROUGE-L_fp16=0.41  ROUGE-L_int4=0.27 — pretty big quality regression.

matt besser: ouch. Did you enable the KV-cache offset fix? We merged a hotfix that adjusts kvcache indexing when vocab maps shift (offset +2 in some conversions). If kvcache reads wrong indices you get truncated/garbled continuation.

hema rao: I didn't. where's that flag/patch?

leo wang: short-term workaround: export with env `REDWOOD_KVCACHE_VOCAB_OFFSET=2`. Long term: run the tokenmap normalizer before conversion: 
```
python tools/tokenmap_fix.py --in vocab.json --out vocab.norm.json --fix-endian --pad-sentinels
./model_convert --from=hf --to=redwood --model=cetus-11b --vocab-map=vocab.norm.json --rotary-merge=headwise --out=cetus-redwood.bin
```

sana li: Also try switching rotary scaling mode. Some checkpoints were trained with per-head rotary scaling. Quick experiment: export with `ROTARY_SCALE_MODE=headwise` and re-quantize with a larger calibration set (e.g., 2000 lines). We saw headwise scaling reduce angle leakage and improved long-context coherence in prior onboarding.

hema rao: ACK — I'll run: `quantize.py --model cetus-redwood.bin --bits 4 --calibrate 2000 --out cetus-int4.bin` with ROTARY_SCALE_MODE=headwise and REDWOOD_KVCACHE_VOCAB_OFFSET=2. Posting numbers after job finishes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Job queued: quantize-cetus11b-int4 (calibrate=2000) — job id q-2026-03-21-17 — estimated 45m.

matt besser: once you have new evals, dump the top 3 failure prompts + logit traces (preferably a small grep of eos/logit spikes). That will tell if it's still token misalignment vs true quantization loss.

hema rao: will do. I'll also run a quick token-level compare script: `python tools/token_align_check.py --fp16 ./cetus-fp16.bin --int4 ./cetus-int4.bin --out diff.tsv` and upload to #eng-ml-perf. Thanks all :pray:

triage-bot: triage: labeled thread `cetus-11b` as "onboarding:blocking" and assigned to @hema rao, @leo wang.
